course_title: IC Design Process: Beginner's Overview to VLSI

slides.title: Welcome to IC Design Process
points: Bridging HDL code to actual silicon circuits.
Overview of VLSI design and manufacturing.
Focus on theory, not coding practices.
slides.speaker_notes: This course, "IC Design Process," demystifies how HDL code translates into physical silicon. We'll explore the VLSI design and manufacturing flow, from RTL to final product. It's a beginner's overview, focusing on core concepts, not specific coding.

slides.title: ICs and Their Evolution
points: IC: Electronic circuits on a tiny semiconductor plate.
SOC: Complete system on a single chip.
From bulky vacuum tubes to compact transistors.
slides.speaker_notes: An Integrated Circuit, or IC, packs electronic circuits onto a tiny silicon plate. A System-on-Chip, SOC, integrates an entire electronic system onto one chip. Circuits evolved from bulky vacuum tubes to compact transistors, setting the stage for integrated designs.

slides.title: Scaling: From SSI to VLSI
points: Modern standard: VLSI (Very Large Scale Integration).
slides.speaker_notes: IC technology rapidly scaled from Small-Scale Integration, SSI, through Medium and Large-Scale Integration, housing billions of transistors by 2008. Today, all advanced IC manufacturing, regardless of transistor count, is simply known as Very Large Scale Integration, or VLSI.

slides.title: Digital Circuit Fundamentals
slides.speaker_notes: Digital circuits process data as binary numbers, represented by voltage states, with transistors acting as fundamental switches. We differentiate combinational circuits, whose output depends solely on current inputs, from sequential circuits, which incorporate memory and thus depend on input history.

slides.title: Gates, Flip-Flops, Transistors
points: Digital circuits composed of logic gates and flip-flops.
Seven basic logic gates (AND, OR, NOT, etc.).
Flip-flops are memory elements, built from gates.
slides.speaker_notes: Digital circuits are built from logic gates and flip-flops. Logic gates perform boolean operations, while flip-flops are essential memory elements storing single bits. Importantly, flip-flops themselves are constructed using various logic gates.

slides.title: The Power of Abstraction
points: Every digital circuit is made of transistors.
Logic gates are made of transistors; flip-flops from gates.
slides.speaker_notes: Ultimately, every digital circuit boils down to a vast number of transistors: gates from transistors, flip-flops from gates. To manage this complexity, Hardware Description Languages, or HDLs, offer an abstract design level, effectively hiding intricate transistor details.
